key_decisions.rationale: Rejects blame of man and parents while preserving divine-work purpose without turning disability into guilt.
key_decisions.before: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned. Rather, this is so that God’s works may be revealed in him.
key_decisions.after: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned. Rather, this happened so that God’s works might be revealed in him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned; rather, he was born blind so that the works of God might be revealed in him.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps plural mission, sender, day-night image, and urgency.
key_decisions.before: We must work the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night is coming when no one can work.
key_decisions.after: We must do the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night is coming when no one can work.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: We must work the works of the one who sent me while it is day; night is coming when no one can work.

key_decisions.rationale: Clarifies leaders, fear, coercive agreement, confession, and exclusion.
key_decisions.before: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jewish authorities, because the authorities had already agreed that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
key_decisions.after: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jewish authorities, who had already agreed that anyone who confessed Jesus as Messiah would be put out of the synagogue.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: His parents said this because they were afraid of the authorities; for the authorities had already agreed that anyone who confessed Jesus to be the Messiah would be put out of the synagogue.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps exact interrogation, solemn demand, and asserted verdict.
key_decisions.before: So they called the man who had been blind a second time and said, “Give glory to God! We know this man is a sinner.”
key_decisions.after: So for a second time they summoned the man who had been blind and told him, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: So for the second time they called the man who had been blind, and they said to him, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps stigmatizing accusation, elitism, and expulsion.
key_decisions.before: They answered him, “You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?” Then they threw him out.
key_decisions.after: They answered him, “You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?” Then they threw him out.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: They answered him, “You were born entirely in sins, and are you trying to teach us?” And they drove him out.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves reversal and metaphor’s relation to physical sight without conflating disability and guilt.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see and those who see may become blind.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said, “For judgment I came into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves metaphorical claim, their asserted sight, and abiding sin while closing Jesus’ reply.
key_decisions.before: Jesus said, “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say, ‘We see,’ so your sin remains.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus told them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now that you say, ‘We see,’ your sin remains.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say, ‘We see.’ Your sin remains.”
